label: exists

evidence.quote:
Dry-run only: three in-process actors (an authorization server and two
protected resource servers standing in for two MCP servers) exchange plain
dicts as if they were HTTP requests and responses. Nothing here reaches a
network.
live mode until run on the host: adapters/live.py has never reached the endpoint from here

finding: Every mechanism the question names is implemented and checked from a transcript rather than from configuration - the 401's protected-resource pointer, protected-resource and authorization-server metadata discovery, PKCE S256 verified before the code is redeemed, a resource indicator on the authorization request, the initial token request and the refresh, an audience check, a single-endpoint streamable transport, and a tool result validated against its declared output schema - and the refresh-omission breakage fails exactly one check, so the gate can say no. But the whole exchange is three in-process actors this repo wrote on both sides of the wire, with nothing reaching a network; the only adapter that can reach a remote surface authenticates with a static bearer token from an environment variable, with no metadata discovery, no resource indicator and no refresh at all, and has never reached an endpoint. So the mechanisms are demonstrated, not in force: this is the aligned mechanism set exercised against itself, while the one real path carries the misaligned anchor's bearer token with no audience binding.
gap: No captured exchange with a remote surface exists and no transport was ever negotiated: adapters/auth_exchange.py simulates the authorization server and both resource servers in process, and adapters/live.py - the only network-capable adapter - sends a fixed bearer token with no OAuth 2.1, PKCE, metadata discovery, resource indicator or refresh. The authorization check is also outside the capability's gate (test.sh contains no reference to it), so nothing forces the mechanisms on the path an agent would actually use. Closing it means the live adapter obtaining its token through the same exchange auth_exchange.py checks, one run against a real remote server recorded including the refresh, and that check wired into test.sh.
